sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: MID-LEVEL SHORT-WAVE TROUGHING IS FORECAST TO UNDERGO SOME STRENGTHENING AS IT PROGRESS EWD FROM THE N CENTRAL U.S. INTO THE GREAT LAKES REGION...S OF A MUCH STRONGER/LARGER VORTEX OVER ERN CANADA. MEANWHILE...SOME MID-LEVEL AMPLIFICATION IS ALSO FORECAST OVER THE WEST...AS A LARGE RIDGE OVER THE ROCKIES EXPANDS NWD ACROSS THE CANADIAN PRAIRIE AHEAD OF A TROUGH PROGGED TO REMAIN JUST OFF THE WRN NOAM COAST. AT THE SURFACE...COLD FRONT SHOULD MOVE VERY SLOWLY EWD ACROSS THE PAC NW AHEAD OF THE WRN TROUGH. MEANWHILE...A SECOND FRONT WILL MOVE SLOWLY EWD ACROSS THE NORTHEAST STATES...AND SEWD ACROSS THE MIDWEST AND CENTRAL PLAINS.

sections.title: SRN UPPER GREAT LAKES/LOWER GREAT LAKES/OH VALLEY AREA
sections.text: THUNDERSTORMS WILL LIKELY BE ONGOING AT THE START OF THE PERIOD ACROSS PARTS OF THE MIDWEST/UPPER GREAT LAKES REGION -- WITH ONE MCS LIKELY MOVING EWD ACROSS LOWER MI AND POSSIBLY A SECOND SHIFTING SEWD ACROSS IA/WRN IL/NERN MO. WITH THE NRN MCS EXPECTED TO CROSS LOWER MI EARLY...IT APPEARS THAT COOLER/MORE STABLE CONDITIONS WILL PREVAIL -- AT LEAST ACROSS THE NRN HALF OF LOWER MI. S OF THE RAIN-COOLED AIR...HEATING/DESTABILIZATION ACROSS THE SRN UPPER GREAT LAKES/MIDWEST/OH VALLEY REGION WILL SUPPORT AFTERNOON RE-DEVELOPMENT/INTENSIFICATION OF CONVECTION. IT APPEARS THAT DEVELOPMENT MAY OCCUR INVOF REMNANT MCS/MCV SHIFTING ACROSS IL...WITH POSSIBLE RE-DEVELOPMENT INTO A BOWING MCS BY MID TO LATE AFTERNOON. OTHER/MORE ISOLATED DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED FARTHER E...IN CONJUNCTION WITH WEAK/SUBTLE VORTICITY MAXIMA EMBEDDED WITHIN THE MODERATELY-STRONG/CYCLONIC WLYS ALOFT. ALONG WITH SOME HAIL THREAT...MAIN SEVERE POTENTIAL WITH THIS CONVECTION WOULD LIKELY BE DAMAGING WINDS -- PARTICULARLY IF A BOWING MCS DOES EVOLVE THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. STORMS SHOULD MOVE ACROSS THE UPPER OH VALLEY/LOWER LAKES REGION THROUGH LATE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING...BEFORE A SLOW WEAKENING TREND IS FORECAST IN

sections.title: PARTS OF THE CENTRAL AND SRN PLAINS
sections.text: GENERALLY WEAK FLOW ALOFT BUT MODERATE DESTABILIZATION ALONG THE TRAILING PORTION OF THE SEWD-MOVING COLD FRONT WILL SUPPORT SCATTERED AFTERNOON THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT ACROSS PARTS OF MO/KS/OK...AND AS FAR WWD AS THE CENTRAL AND SRN HIGH PLAINS. WHILE SHEAR SHOULD SUPPORT NO MORE THAT MULTICELL ORGANIZATION...A FEW STRONGER STORMS MAY PRODUCE HAIL AND BRIEF GUSTY WINDS. ..GOSS.. 06/27/2010

sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST EWD ACROSS THE GREAT LAKES AND OH VALLEY
sections.text: TWO SEPARATE MESOSCALE SYSTEMS HAVE PERSISTED THROUGH THE EARLY MORNING HOURS...ONE WHICH IS LIKELY SLIGHTLY ELEVATED OVER LOWER MI...AND THE OTHER WHICH IS PROGRESSING EWD/SEWD THROUGH SRN/ERN IA...NRN MO AND WRN/CNTRL IL. THE FORMER WILL CONTINUE EWD TODAY INTO SWRN ONTARIO WITH SOME POTENTIAL FOR MARGINALLY SEVERE WIND/HAIL ACROSS LOWER MI THIS MORNING. MEANWHILE...GUST FRONT AND MCV ASSOCIATED WITH THE LATTER WILL LIKELY SERVE AS FOCI FOR GRADUAL STORM INTENSIFICATION TODAY ACROSS PARTS OF IL/IND AND SRN LOWER MI. MESOSCALE FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH THESE REMNANT CONVECTIVE SYSTEMS WILL BE AUGMENTED BY INCREASED HEIGHT FALLS/DYNAMIC FORCING FOR ASCENT ATTENDANT TO AMPLIFYING MIDLEVEL TROUGH WHICH WILL PROGRESS SEWD THROUGH THE UPPER MS VALLEY INTO UPPER GREAT LAKES...AND WEAKER PRECEDING IMPULSE NOW OVER THE ERN DAKOTAS INTO MN. AMBIENT WARM SECTOR AIR MASS REMAINS QUITE MOIST /I.E. DEW POINTS IN THE LOWER 70S/ THIS MORNING AHEAD OF WRN MCS AND ALONG AND S OF OUTFLOW BOUNDARY/SYNOPTIC FRONT ORIENTED IN WNW-ESE FASHION FROM SRN WI/NRN IL INTO NRN OH. WHILE MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES ARE NOT FORECAST TO BE PARTICULARLY STEEP...DAYTIME HEATING IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER

sections.title: OZARKS INTO THE CNTRL/SRN PLAINS
sections.text: A HOT AND MOIST AIR MASS WILL EXIST ALONG AND SOUTH OF SURFACE FRONT TODAY WITH MLCAPE INCREASING TO 2000-3000 J/KG. THE PRESENCE OF THE FRONT IN CONCERT WITH A FAIRLY WELL DEFINED VORTICITY MAXIMUM/MCV CURRENTLY MOVING THROUGH CNTRL KS SHOULD FOSTER SCATTERED...DIURNAL STORM DEVELOPMENT TO THE SW OF ONGOING STORMS OVER NRN/CNTRL MO. REGION WILL REMAIN TO THE S OF STRONGER MIDLEVEL WIND FIELD ATTENDANT TO N-CNTRL CONUS SYSTEM WITH PULSE AND MULTICELL STORMS LIKELY BEING THE DOMINANT MODES. NONETHELESS...THE STRONGER STORMS WILL REMAIN CAPABLE OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND PERHAPS SOME HAIL THROUGH THIS EVENING. ..MEAD/HURLBUT.. 06/27/2010

sections.title: OH VALLEY TO PA/NY THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: A SERIES OF EMBEDDED SHORTWAVE TROUGHS OVER NRN PLAINS AND ADJACENT PRAIRIE PROVINCES WILL ROTATE ESEWD AROUND THE SRN PERIPHERY OF A DEEP CLOSED LOW NEAR JAMES BAY. THE MIDLEVEL WAVE WILL BE PRECEDED BY A DEEPENING SURFACE CYCLONE THAT IS EXPECTED TO MOVE EWD FROM WI/LOWER MI TODAY TO THE SAINT LAWRENCE VALLEY BY EARLY MONDAY. IN ADVANCE OF THE SURFACE CYCLONE...THE UNSTABLE WARM SECTOR IS ALREADY ESTABLISHED ACROSS THE OH VALLEY...AND WILL SPREAD NEWD ACROSS PA/SRN NY THROUGH THIS EVENING. A REMNANT MCV FROM OVERNIGHT CONVECTION WILL MOVE EWD FROM NRN IL/SRN WI ACROSS NRN INDIANA/SRN LOWER MI AND NRN OH THROUGH THIS AFTERNOON...ALONG THE NRN EDGE OF THE WARM SECTOR. A BELT OF ENHANCED /30-40 KT/ LOW-MIDLEVEL WLY FLOW WITH THE MCV...AND A STRONGLY UNSTABLE WARM SECTOR WITH MLCAPE VALUES UP TO 4000 J/KG...WILL CONTRIBUTE TO A FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR INTENSIFICATION OF THE CONVECTION NOW OVER NW INDIANA. WIND PROFILES WILL SUPPORT BOTH ORGANIZED MULTICELL CLUSTERS AND SOME EMBEDDED SUPERCELL STRUCTURES...WITH DAMAGING WINDS THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREAT. ISOLATED LARGE HAIL WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE...ALONG WITH A LOW-PROBABILITY THREAT FOR A TORNADO /PRIMARILY WITH STORMS INTERACTING WIT

sections.title: MO TO OK/NW TX THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: THE SURFACE COLD FRONT /ASSOCIATED WITH THE AMPLIFYING NRN STREAM TROUGH NEAR THE GREAT LAKES/ WILL MOVE SLOWLY SWD/SEWD ACROSS ERN NM/W TX...NW OK...ERN KS...NW MO...AND IA DURING THE DAY. THE FRONT /AND A PRE-FRONTAL WIND SHIFT/GRAVITY WAVE JUST SE OF THE I-44 CORRIDOR IN OK AND MO/ WILL FOCUS THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON...WITH COVERAGE ENHANCED DOWNSTREAM FROM REMNANT MIDLEVEL VORTICITY CENTERS OVER NW TX AND NE KS. DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR WILL REMAIN WEAK TO THE S OF THE MAIN BELT OF WLYS /ESPECIALLY FROM OK SWWD/. HOWEVER...DAYTIME HEATING WILL CONTRIBUTE TO AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF 2000-3000 J/KG AND SOME POTENTIAL FOR SPORADIC DOWNBURSTS AND MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL WITH THE MORE INTENSE STORMS. ..THOMPSON/SMITH.. 06/27/2010
